- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially when recent history shows upward momentum.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes in the history (e.g., after 60+ values), often overshooting by 5–15%.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Shows strong mean reversion bias: overcorrects downward after recent highs, then fails to recover fully.
- Underestimates late-period (last 5–10 days) price increases, especially when true values show accelerating upward trends.
- Sensitive to recent volatility: if last 5 days show high variance, model tends to over-smooth, underestimating true volatility-driven spikes.
- Often fails to capture “rebound” after sharp declines — underestimates recovery magnitude and timing.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 10 days; later days show diminishing error, suggesting model adapts better to longer-term trends.
